headline: Every source card needs a path back to the passage.
copy: The link layer keeps citation, family, anchor, status, rights posture, and boundary together so learners can inspect where an answer is standing.
boundary: Deep links are prototype anchors until verified editions and passage rights are approved.

records.title: Steadiness in action
records.allowedUse: Use for calm path, practice, and learner action cards.
records.boundary: Reflection support only, not therapy, diagnosis, or ritual instruction.
records.summary: The source candidate supports steadiness while acting, with caution about clinging to results.

records.title: Time and destruction
records.allowedUse: Use for Oppenheimer-source clarification and category correction.
records.boundary: Do not call it a direct Vedic quote or a four-Veda passage.
records.summary: This is the commonly cited source family behind the Oppenheimer line in popular culture.

records.title: Disciplined speech
records.allowedUse: Use for speech-before-reply drafts and conversation companion.
records.boundary: Do not make the app an authority over personal relationships.
records.summary: The passage supports truthful, gentle, beneficial speech as a practice discipline.

records.title: Stewardship and restraint
records.allowedUse: Use for restraint, ownership, and simplicity reflections after edition review.
records.boundary: Do not use it as a proof text for modern economic claims.
records.summary: The opening passage is often read around restraint, belonging, and sacred presence.

records.title: Self knowledge boundary
records.allowedUse: Use as a source candidate for humility around knowledge after review.
records.boundary: Do not turn this into mystical certainty or guru authority.
records.summary: The passage is commonly associated with limits of mere instruction or intellect in realizing the Self.

linkRules.title: Stable anchor
linkRules.copy: Use a human-readable citation anchor that can survive UI changes.

linkRules.title: Visible category
linkRules.copy: Show source family beside every link so Gita, Veda, Upanishad, and commentary do not blur.

linkRules.title: Copyable packet
linkRules.copy: Let reviewers copy link id, citation, family, status, rights, and boundary in one move.
